intro: Talking about your job and schedule, and getting through a short interview.
p.experiencia.consejo: You say «tener experiencia» and «mucha» or «poca experiencia». The x sounds ks.
p.oficina.consejo: In Spain the c sounds «th»: o-fi-THI-na. You work «en una oficina».
p.puesto.consejo: It is a job post: «un puesto de camarero». It is also a stall in a market.
p.a jornada completa.consejo: You work the whole normal schedule, usually about eight hours a day.
p.horario.consejo: The h is silent: o-RA-ryo. You say «un horario de nueve a seis».
p.sueldo.consejo: It is paid each month. «Salario» means almost the same.
p.empresa.consejo: You work «en una empresa». There are small, medium and large ones.
p.entrevista.consejo: You say «tener una entrevista» or «hacer una entrevista». The v sounds b.
p.currículum.consejo: It has an accent on the í. You say «mandar el currículum» to a company.
p.a tiempo parcial.consejo: You work few hours. The opposite is «a jornada completa».
p.estoy en paro.consejo: It is very common in Spain. «Paro» comes from «parar» and is also the state benefit.
p.contratar.consejo: It comes from «contrato». The company hires, the worker is hired.
p.trabajo.consejo: The j sounds h: tra-BA-ho. It is also the verb in yo: «trabajo en una oficina».
b1.texto:
To say what you do: **soy** ingeniera. **Trabajo de** camarero. Use **trabajar de / como** + profession and **trabajar en** + place: trabajo **en** una empresa.

Your conditions: tengo un **horario** de nueve a seis. Trabajo **a tiempo parcial** or **a jornada completa**.

To say how long you have been somewhere: **llevo** tres años **en** esta empresa; **llevo** un año **trabajando** en una oficina.

Looking for work: **estoy en paro**; mando el **currículum**; tengo una **entrevista**. A company **contrata** someone for a **puesto**.

In a formal interview, **usted** is used: **¿Qué experiencia tiene?** **¿Cuándo puede empezar?**
b2.f1.texto: I worked as a waiter for three years.
b2.f2.texto: Now I have been working in an office for a year.
b2.f3.texto: Why do you want to change jobs?
b2.f4.texto: I am looking for a full-time position.
b2.f5.texto: The schedule is from nine to six.
b4.texto:
Each preposition says something different:

- **trabajar de** + profession: trabajo **de** camarero (my trade).
- **trabajar en** + place: trabajo **en** una oficina, **en** una empresa.

To say how long you have been doing something:

- **llevar + time + en + place**: **llevo** tres años **en** esta empresa.
- **llevar + time + gerund**: **llevo** un año **trabajando** aquí.

For a finished past, the indefinido: **trabajé** tres años de camarero.
b4.e0.texto: I work as a waiter in a small café.
b4.e1.texto: I have been at this company for three years.
b4.e2.texto: I am unemployed and looking for work.
b5.f0.texto: The company building shines under the morning sun.
b5.f1.texto: Pablo crosses the glass door with a firm step.
b5.f2.texto: A friendly receptionist hands him a blue card.
b5.f3.texto: The lift goes up in silence to the fifth floor.
b5.f4.texto: From the corridor you can hear a murmur of keyboards and voices.
b5.f5.texto: The boss waits seated behind a clean desk.
b5.f6.texto: On the desk there is a notebook, a cup and a clock.
b5.f7.texto: Pablo breathes deeply and answers in a calm voice.
b5.f8.texto: His hands stop trembling over the new CV.
b5.f9.texto: The boss smiles and shakes his hand at the end.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Well done! «Trabajar de» + profession says your trade.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «En» goes with the place: «trabajo en un bar».
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Trabajé un camarero» makes no sense: the preposition is missing.
b6.pregunta: Choose the preposition for the profession.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes! «Jornada completa» is the whole normal schedule.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Tiempo parcial» is only part of the day.
b7.pregunta: Which expression means working the whole day?
b8.frase: Llevo un año trabajando en una oficina
b8.traduccion: I have been working in an office for a year
b9.frase: Llevo un año ____ en una oficina.
b9.o1.refuerzo: The infinitive does not go with «llevo un año».
b9.o2.refuerzo: «Trabajo» is already conjugated; a gerund is needed here.
b9.titulo: I have been for a year
b10.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I'm looking for a job».
b11.o0.refuerzo: Exactly! It is the usual form in Spain.
b11.o1.refuerzo: Holidays are a break from work, not unemployment.
b11.o2.refuerzo: That would be «tiempo parcial». In paro you do not work.
b12.o0.refuerzo: Well done! «Usted» goes with the verb in third person.
b12.o1.refuerzo: «Tienes» is for tú; it does not fit with «usted».
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Tengo» is yo; she asks about you.
p.quinto.consejo: Ordinal number. The stress is on KIN.
p.teclados.consejo: Plural of «teclado». The stress is on KLA.
p.jefa.consejo: Feminine form of «jefe». The j sounds like h.
p.temblar.consejo: Infinitive. The stress falls on the last syllable, LAR.
